I really like a lot of the new art, but there is always some critiquing to do.

 

Legacy's new costume is interesting, but it bothers me for some reason. I think it is the gloves, I don't know why ut the fact he is wearing gloves is just.... odd to me. Maybe because it implies it is a one-piece costume? Anyways I do like it it just seems strange to me to see LEgacy in that suit.

 

I love Bunker's new suit, despite the off perspective leg, for one simple reason. It is clearly the precursor to the Tactics Bunker suit built by Tachyon and them. This is great for all the story reasons. Bunker just stopped working for the military and they cut off his access to the suit, this is the prototype of the new suit to come, which helps explain some of the roughness of the design.

 

Tachyon running next to the bullet train is cool. The costume itself isn't all that amazing or different except in color scheme, butI love the visor she has, defintely a stylish upgrade from her old HUD goggles.

 

Ra is awesome, he definetly looks very regal and it is a great send off for one of the base heroes. R.I.P. Dr. Washington.

 

Absolute Zero's outfit is... honestly I'm torn. It looks rough, it looks incomplete. I can see all the negatives about it. But, looking at the frost leaking around the joints I get the feeling this is another rough prototype, something thrown together because the old suit got wrecked and he needed something quickly from the lab. I also do sometimes enjoy the triangle of light face plate, makes him look sort of alien.

 

Wraith... whoo boy. When I first saw it I loved it. I love the electro-shock knuckles and the Spite style mask. So much potential story in that choice. The white circles in her leggings didn't bother me at first, but the more I've seen it the more it bothers me. The clincher came when someone photoshopped a version that replaced the circles with the red color of the suit. It looked so, so much better to me. I think this is one of the few times I think we should work to have Adam change a design. Maybe the circles would look better if they were grey, or purple or matched the color scheme, but I definetly think the design needs to be altered. It just doesn't work as well as it potentially could.

posts.name: Estelindis
posts.cooked:
To provide people with the exact quote, Adam said as follows: "It's a reference to specific feudal Japanese clothing.  It was done usually with more billowy fabric (and more revealing as such) to allow more freedom of movement."  I mean, sure, it would've been more revealing if people wore nothing under it, but that's not how it's worn.

I find that the hakama allows good freedom of movement and nice back support.  In terms of stretchiness, it's of course not stretchy in the way of modern fabrics, as you say, but each hakama can fit a wide range of different sizes of people.  You order it by height, not waist size (unless you're unusually big around the waist).  The long belt can be wrapped around the waist more or fewer times, however big or small one's waist is, assuming one isn't so large that one can't fit into the hakama at all.  But with the Wraith's outfit being fairly tight and form-fitting, I can't imagine that the holes at the hips give additional freedom of movement. 

Anyway, it might be a moot point, as frankly the bandages of her original outfit aren't very practical either.  In particular, I have no idea how her bandage facemask works.  It must wrap around the back of her head to stay up, but her hair is hanging loose there...  So it's possible that we may have to accept a certain lack of realism in general.

Belle Sorciere:

My reason for what I said is that destroying everything across the board isn't really all that much fun.

I tend to disagree, because every time Dawn does her Devastating Aurora I feel it ends up being especially thematic.  The heroes have build up to destroy her - and she flips the board.

Coming right after the environment play makes it seem especially thematic to the game, like Dawn is reacting to the situation in a way that accounts for more than the heroes. When you pull out "Lost in Time," "Propulsion Systems," "Self-Destruct Sequence," or the like, it seems like Citizen Dawn has had enough of this situation where she could lose just as much as the heroes do, and she decides to JUST BLOW EVERYTHING UP.

I agree that sometimes it can be brutal and you lose the game in the end, but that's the way it is sometimes and that's one of the reasons why Citizen Dawn is a difficult villain to fight. I'm glad "those cards" are in there, because they force the players to re-evaluate their strategies in a way that "the villain deals each target H - 2 melee damage" or "reduce damage to all villain targets by 1" do not. The best games are the ones that go back and forth and the heroes win in the end after a ferocious battle!
